# Figure AI

Fetched: 2026-07-16
URL: https://www.figure.ai/

## Page inventory

1. Homepage (www.figure.ai) - Hero/product introduction with newsletter signup. ~2-3 minutes to scan.
2. Figure 03 (www.figure.ai/figure) - Product specification page with technical specs and capabilities overview. ~2 minutes.
3. Helix (www.figure.ai/helix) - AI system positioning with video demonstrations. ~3 minutes.
4. Company (www.figure.ai/company) - Mission, values, product evolution timeline, team credentials. ~2 minutes.
5. News/Blog (www.figure.ai/news) - Article index with 18 posts dating Feb 2025 to July 2026. Each article 1-3 minutes.
6. Careers section - Implied in navigation; not directly fetched but referenced in footer.

## Homepage section order

1. Navigation header with links: Figure 03, Helix, Company, News, Careers
2. Hero: "The future of home help is here" + "Figure 03 is a general purpose humanoid robot for every day" + video link
3. AI Intelligence section: "The intelligence behind Figure 03" explaining Helix navigation capabilities
4. Product Capabilities: "Understands your home like you do" with human-shaped, AI-powered positioning
5. Team Credibility: "The team bringing impossible ideas to life" with 100-year combined experience claim
6. Newsletter signup: "Keep up with us" with email capture
7. Footer: Social links, navigation, copyright, contact form

## Proof placement

**Figure 03 Specifications** (Same page, dedicated block):
- Height: 5'8", Weight: 61KG, Payload: 20KG, Runtime: 5HR, Speed: 1.2M/S
- Evidence: Technical spec sheet presentation; no source attribution

**Helix Performance Metrics** (Separate news article, not on product page):
- Logistics package handling: 4.05 seconds/package (down from ~5.0s); 95% barcode success rate
- With 60-hour training data: 4.31 seconds (58% throughput improvement), 94.4% accuracy (up from 88.2%)
- Evidence: Controlled evaluations with Figure 1 and Figure 2 charts referenced; presented in dedicated news article dated June 7, 2025
- Gap: No independent validation; no third-party benchmarking

**Figure 02 Real-World Deployment** (News article):
- "Contributed to the assembly of 30,000 cars at BMW last year"
- Evidence: Single quantified claim; no breakdown of tasks, timeline, or performance impact

**Figure 03 BMW Deployment** (News article):
- Location: Hall 52 at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg; Date: June 30, 2026
- Capabilities: Logistics workflow, dynamic whole-body control, grasping, cart pulling
- Evidence: None. Announced capabilities lack performance metrics, error rates, or comparative data. Announcement lacks proof of operational results.

**Team Credentials** (Repeated across 3+ pages):
- "Over 100 years of combined AI & humanoid experience"
- Evidence: None provided. Claim appears on homepage, company page, and Helix page without breakdown by individual, role, or credential type.

## Claim qualification

When evidence is absent, Figure AI uses three patterns:

1. **Future capability positioning**: "Figure takes care of household tasks like laundry, cleaning, and doing dishes, all autonomously." (Assertion without timeline or proof specification)

2. **Design aspiration language**: "F.03 was reimagined for home use with a softer look and feel to better suit everyday living." (Subjective framing rather than tested outcome)

3. **Ability claim without metrics**: "Helix is designed to reason like a human" and "consider and perform tasks on its own, without following a script." (Cognitive claim; no behavioral tests provided)

4. **Vague partnership language**: "Catalyst Brands to Scale Humanoid Operations" (no specifics on scale, timeline, or success criteria)

## Measurements

Heading word counts:
- Main hero: 7 words
- Product subheading: 10 words
- Section headings: 5-8 words
- Helix primary: 23 words
- Secondary sections: 3-7 words

Body copy word counts:
- Typical paragraph: 12-18 words
- Longer descriptions: 16-23 words

Shortest copy: "F.03 Battery" (2 words), "Move Fast & Be Technically Fearless" (5 words)
Longest copy: Helix description at 23 words; news headlines stay under 12 words

Pattern: Short, punchy headings (5-8 words for sections); medium-length body copy (12-18 words); technical claims in longer form (15-23 words)

## Type and color

**Typography**: Sans-serif throughout; clean, modern tech aesthetic. Font family specifics not directly accessible via rendered page inspection.

**Color Palette**: 
- Background: Neutral (appears to be white/light gray on light mode based on CDN image paths)
- Text: High contrast dark text on light backgrounds
- Accent colors: Minimal visible color information extracted; appears to follow tech industry minimalism (likely neutral accents with subtle interaction states)
- CTAs: Standard interactive affordances (links styled for clarity)

**Visual hierarchy**: Large hero image of metallic humanoid robot (full-body shot, optimized WebP, responsive dual images for desktop/mobile). Technical specs presented in structured table format. Section cards use consistent spacing and alignment. No visible decorative elements; functional visual design focused on product imagery.

## Conversion path

1. **Entry point**: Homepage hero section with video link
2. **Navigation paths**: 
   - "Explore Figure 03" leads to product detail page with specs
   - "See Helix in Logistics" leads to Helix page with video demonstrations
   - "Explore Helix's AI System" leads to Helix page
3. **Action items**: 
   - Newsletter email signup (no paywall, no product sale)
   - Video consumption (full videos available via "Watch Now" and "Full Video" links)
   - News articles (public reading; no gating)
   - Careers section (implied job listings)
4. **What reader gets first**: Product specification, AI capability overview, and evidence of real-world deployment (via news articles)
5. **No purchase path shown**: Figure 03 not for sale publicly; commercial inquiries require direct contact (implied but not explicitly linked from main site)

## Distinctive

**Multi-generational product narrative with purposeful evolution**: Figure AI stages its messaging across three generations (F.01: foundational 2023, F.02: workforce-focused 2024-2025, F.03: home-focused late 2025+). Each generation is presented with a specific job-to-be-done rather than incremental feature lists. This progression creates a through-line narrative of increasing readiness and market expansion. No other major robotics company websites examined here emphasize generational purpose so explicitly.

## Noise

**"Over 100 years of combined AI & humanoid experience" claim repeated without substantiation**: This phrase appears identically on the homepage, company page, and Helix page. It is never broken down by individual team members, credential type, source company, or domain area. The claim functions as authority-by-accumulation without providing measurable credibility signals. It is category noise because every hardware company at this stage repeats credential claims without specificity.

## Not accessible

Careers section was not directly fetched (no role listings retrieved). Pricing and commercial availability were sourced from third-party robotics review sites, not from figure.ai pages. Figure 03 purchase path not visible on site (product not yet for public sale; partnership model dominates).
